Route Notes: Travel to Liechtenstein, cable car to Gaflei, final gear check, early dinner
Gentle prologue. Mostly downhill through Vaduz and the Rhine Valley. Ideal day to settle into trail rhythm and test packs.
Valley walking followed by first sustained climb. Early finish for recovery.
First major alpine pass (Foopass, 2,223 m). Excellent lunch stop at the pass.
Richetlipass. Steep ascent and technical descent. Finish with funicular to car-free Braunwald.
Traverse Switzerland’s largest alp (Urnerboden) before finishing directly on Klausenpass. Sunset views from hotel terrace.
Long descent. Waterfalls and classic Uri scenery. Easy recovery day.
Familiar terrain. Use Brüsti cable car to avoid unnecessary climbing. Lunch at Blackenalp.
Recovery day. Explore Engelberg or take train to Lucerne. Laundry, good food, proper rest.
Short but steep climb over Jochpass. One of the most beautiful overnight locations on the route.
High alpine traverse then long descent into Meiringen.
Grosse Scheidegg. First major views of the Eiger.
Kleine Scheidegg beneath the Eiger north face. One of Switzerland’s iconic hiking days.
Easy day. Visit Trümmelbach Falls. Use gondola/train to Mürren and enjoy the panorama.
Sefinenfurgge (2,612 m). One of the most spectacular stages of the Via Alpina.
Hohtürli (2,778 m), highest point on the route. Lunch at Blüemlisalphütte. Oeschinensee on descent.
Take Allmenalp cable car. Cross Bunderchrinde into Adelboden.
Easier recovery day over Hahnenmoos Pass.
Long scenic day into the French-speaking part of Switzerland.
Swiss National Day. Excellent cheese village and limited accommodation.
Relaxed day. Long lunch and afternoon recovery before final climb.
Final major ascent. Outstanding views of Lake Geneva, Mont Blanc and the Alps.
Final descent to Lake Geneva. Château de Chillon and Montreux lakeside celebration.
Suggested Accommodation: Fairmont Le Montreux Palace or similar
